newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices rise on improved demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices rise on improved demand.

text.p: Sugar prices rose on Monday on improved demand on fears of a rise in the administered price of the supplies made through cheap ration shops, dealers said.
They said the market was expecting a rise of 1.25-1.50 rupees per kg from the present 9.05 rupees per kg.

The market, where sugar is also available from a free sale quota, turned firm as sugar mills sold limited stocks, dealers said. Under a dual pricing system, mills sell 60 percent of their production in the free market and supply the remainder at a government-fixed price.
Ready sugar S-30 rose 5.0 rupees to 1,250/1,290 per quintal and M-30 gained 9.0 rupees to 1,300/1,380 per quintal. Sugar mill delivery was up from 1,190/1,200 to 1,200/1,215
